summary: Describes using elliptic curve algorithms, ECDH with EnvelopedData and ECDSA with SignedData, for the CMS encrypted key package content type. It extends RFC 6033 and is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC explains how existing elliptic-curve algorithms can be used with CMS encrypted key packages. ECDH and ECDSA are optional, but implementations that support either must support keys on the P-256 curve.

subtitle: Conventions for using elliptic-curve algorithms with CMS encrypted key packages.

tldr.problem: The CMS encrypted key package specifications need conventions for using existing elliptic-curve algorithms.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC allows standard ECDH with EnvelopedData and ECDSA with SignedData, and requires support for P-256 keys when either is supported.
tldr.outcome: RFC 6161 defines no new algorithms and updates RFC 6033 with these conventions.

facts.label: Required curve when using ECDH or ECDSA

today: RFC 6161 is a Proposed Standard and updates RFC 6033. The unit metadata records no RFC that obsoletes RFC 6161.

sections.title: Elliptic-Curve Algorithms in CMS
sections.content: RFC 6161 describes conventions for using elliptic-curve algorithms with the CMS EncryptedKeyPackage content type. It covers CMS EnvelopedData and SignedData and amends RFC 6033. It does not define new algorithms; it refers to algorithms already defined elsewhere.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo says how existing elliptic-curve tools fit into CMS encrypted key packages. It extends an earlier specification without creating new algorithms.

sections.title: ECDH and ECDSA Options
sections.content: When an implementation uses key agreement with EnvelopedData, it MAY support standard ECDH rather than cofactor ECDH. If an implementation encapsulates an EncryptedKeyPackage with SignedData, it MAY support ECDSA as its signature scheme. Both algorithm choices are optional under this memo.
sections.plainLanguage: An implementation may use ECDH to agree on a key for enveloped data and may use ECDSA to sign a package. The memo does not require either choice.

sections.title: Required Curve Support
sections.content: The RFC says public-key certificates are the easiest way to implement SignedData and EnvelopedData. If an implementation supports ECDSA or ECDH, it MUST support keys on the P-256 curve.
sections.plainLanguage: ECDH and ECDSA remain optional. If an implementation supports either one, it must also support keys on the P-256 curve.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says that the security considerations in the referenced certificate, CMS and elliptic-curve specifications apply. It does not define separate security rules for these conventions.
sections.plainLanguage: Implementations must also follow the security guidance in the related CMS, certificate and elliptic-curve specifications.
